column1: # Declared relations between clause fingerprints, over the corpus formed by every clause's own
# fixtures. tests/test_occasion_algebra.py computes each fingerprint's extension and fails on a
# relation that is NOT declared here, on a declared relation that no longer holds, and on a live
# clause whose fingerprint matches nothing.
# Overlap is DECLARED, never condemned. Most rows below are several clauses reading ONE effect --
# a rewrite is a patch is an in-place edit, on the worktree -- and a check that condemned
# subsumption outright would fire on those for no defect. A gate firing on
# lookalikes is itself Asymmetric: the noise does not heal, the gate gets disabled, and its real
# catches go with it.
# RELATION is read left-to-right: A SUPERSET B means every element matching B also matches A.
# WITNESS is an element of the shared extension -- a command for a command fingerprint, the
# canonical JSON of an observation record for an effect fingerprint -- and must still be matched
# by BOTH, so a fingerprint edit breaks the row rather than silently re-pointing it.
# ONE REFUSAL NAMES EVERY CLAUSE REFUSING. Since occasions became effects, a shared occasion is
# not a double denial: the next call after the effect is refused once, naming each clause owed,
# and each guard pays its own. tests/test_occasion_algebra.py measures exactly that per row.
